A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the carbohydrate metabolism in the two plants studied showed similar trends in the two phases of dormancies, viz. peak period of rest (1-10 DAH) and presprouting (10-70 DAH).

the carbohydrate metabolism in the yam tubers and turmeric rhizomes is regulated by the enzymes involved in the starch degradation, glycolysis and the enzymes of the TCA cycle and oxidative pentone phosphate pathway.
the dormancy of yam and turmeric is due to the reduced activity of the key enzymes of starch degradation and the increased activities of the enzymes of sugar metabolism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dormancy period in these plants may be divided into peak period and pre-sprouting period, which may be useful for the management of these crops in the field.
, the dormancy period in both these species can be divided into two phases, viz. peak of rest and prespouting.
, the enzymes involved in carbohydrate metabolism are good markers for monitoring the dormancy and presprouting periods of yam and turmeric.
